claims.text: MOA: bactericidal; inhibit bact DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (suppress RNA synth).
claims.quote: The rifamycins are bactericidal antibiotics; they inhibit bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, suppressing RNA synthesis.

claims.text: Treats: RIF: most gram (+) and some gram (-) bacteria and Mycobacterium; resistance develops rapidly, so it's rarely used alone.
claims.quote: Rifampin is active against Most gram-positive and some gram-negative bacteria Mycobacterium species Resistance develops rapidly, so rifampin is rarely used alone.

claims.text: Know: RIF (w other abx): TB, atypical mycobacteria, leprosy (w dapsone), staph infect of bone, prosthetic valves or joints.
claims.quote: Rifampin is used with other antibiotics for Tuberculosis Atypical mycobacterial infection (rifampin is active against many nontuberculous mycobacteria, but rapidly growing mycobacteria, such as Mycobacterium fortuitum, M. chelonae, or M. abscessus, are naturally resistant) Leprosy (with dapsone with or without clofazimine) Staphylococcal infections, including osteomyelitis, prosthetic valve endocarditis, and infections involving foreign bodies such as a prosthetic joint (with other antistaphylococcal antibiotics)

claims.text: Know: RIF alone: ppx of close contacts of meningococcal or H. flu type b meningitis.
claims.quote: Rifampin can be used alone for prophylaxis of close contacts of patients with meningococcal meningitis or Haemophilus influenzae type b meningitis.

claims.text: Know: rifabutin = preferred over RIF w ART (less CYP450 induction).
claims.quote: However, if patients are receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), rifabutin is preferred because it is less likely to induce cytochrome P-450 metabolic enzymes that lower serum levels of protease inhibitors and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors.

claims.text: Know: rifapentine: latent TB, always w INH as a 12-week once-weekly regimen.
claims.quote: PRIFTIN must always be used in combination with isoniazid as a 12-week once-weekly regimen for the treatment of latent tuberculosis infection

claims.text: Know: rifaximin: poorly absorbed PO (stays in the gut); traveler's diarrhea (E. coli). ⍉for invasive enteric pathogens (Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter).
claims.quote: Rifaximin is a derivative of rifamycin that is poorly absorbed after oral administration; 97% is recovered primarily unchanged in feces. Rifaximin can be used for empiric treatment of Traveler’s diarrhea, which is caused primarily by enterotoxigenic and enteroaggregative Escherichia coli Rifaximin is not known to be effective for diarrhea due to enteric pathogens other than E. coli. Because rifaximin is not systemically absorbed, it should not be used to treat infectious diarrhea caused by invasive enteric bacterial pathogens (eg, Shigella species, Salmonella species, Campylobacter species).

claims.text: Know: rifaximin also: hepatic encephalopathy and IBS.
claims.quote: Rifaximin may also be used for the treatment of Portosystemic (hepatic) encephalopathy Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
XIFAXAN is contraindicated in patients with a hypersensitivity to rifaximin, any of the rifamycin antimicrobial agents, or any of the components in XIFAXAN.

claims.text: Preg: RIF/rifapentine: some animal risk (teratogenicity), ⍉adequate human studies. CDC doesn't consider RIF a CI to breastfeed.
claims.quote: Animal reproduction studies with rifampin or rifapentine show some risk (ie, teratogenicity) at medication levels less than or equal to those typically achieved in humans. No adequate and well-controlled studies with either medication have been done in pregnant women. Because of potential tumorigenicity shown in animal studies, the manufacturer does not recommend use of rifampin during breastfeeding. However, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) does not consider rifampin a contraindication to breastfeeding; a decision to stop breastfeeding or to stop the medication should be made depending on the importance of the medication to the mother.
claims.locator: Use of Rifamycins During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Caution: hepatitis (most serious; ↑ w INH or PZA); GI upset; CNS effects; myelosuppression.
claims.quote: Adverse effects of rifamycins include Hepatitis (most serious) Gastrointestinal disturbances Central nervous system effects Myelosuppression Hepatitis occurs much more often when isoniazid or pyrazinamide is used concurrently with rifampin.

claims.text: Caution: RIF, rifabutin and rifapentine turn urine, saliva, sweat, sputum and tears reddish orange; soft contact lenses may stain permanently. Rifabutin: uveitis.
claims.quote: Rifabutin can cause dose-dependent unilateral or bilateral uveitis. Less serious adverse effects are common; they include heartburn, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Rifampin, rifabutin, and rifapentine can cause temporary reddish orange discoloration of urine, saliva, sweat, sputum, and tears. Soft contact lenses may be permanently discolored.

claims.text: Caution: RIF = a potent CYP450 inducer: may ↓ effect of many drugs (eg, warfarin, hormonal contraceptives, protease inhibitors, fluconazole, phenytoin, digoxin, corticosteroids).
claims.quote: Rifampin interacts with many medications because it is a potent inducer of hepatic cytochrome P-450 (CYP450) microsomal enzymes. Rifampin accelerates elimination and thereby may decrease the effectiveness of the following medications: angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, atovaquone, barbiturates, beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, chloramphenicol, clarithromycin, oral and systemic hormone contraceptives, corticosteroids, cyclosporine, dapsone, digoxin, doxycycline, fluconazole, haloperidol, itraconazole, ketoconazole, the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors delavirdine and nevirapine, opioid analgesics, phenytoin, protease inhibitors, quinidine, sulfonylureas, tacrolimus, theophylline, thyroxine, tocainide, tricyclic antidepressants, voriconazole, warfarin, and zidovudine.
